reviewed_arguments: Compactly supported distributions on the boundary have a proved finite normal-jet representation. The weighted Fourier function recovers each coefficient through an invertible compact moment matrix; the tail integral excludes exactly all indices at least m.

The entire positive Gram matrix retains cross terms and the original Fourier constant. Both directions of the supported-source norm and every coefficient space are proved, including tangential dimension zero and global preferred transfers.

The original left-ordered polynomial gives the complete boundary source with every normal coefficient derivative, binomial factor and phase. Its full freeze-defect matrix, kernel criterion and separate q-th weighted gain are explicit.
Variable density factors give bounded invertible triangular changes by the same full delta-product formula. All actual bundle matrices remain in place.
The complete upper model matches every requested normal coefficient on both tails. Finite real-parameter Taylor remainders and the complementary cone give all differentiated mixed estimates.

A directly tested Laplace integral fixes the kernel phase, factorial and normal support. Compact tangential localization, normal properness changes, separated kernels and preferred global transfers give an exact finite decomposition.
The volume argument defines zero extension through normal L2. The model uses any full extension by its support, while the remainder has the exact weight dominance for every nonnegative normal order.

Each supported delta derivative is handled by the actual operator AD^b and a finite subtraction chosen for the requested normal order. The full coefficient norm controls the resulting layer and every one-sided trace bound.

Both original error bundles and both ordered error-layer products retain all q-th source gains, every normal trace order and every prescribed boundary-row order. Finite errors are not declared smooth.

Four complete exercises verify the full three-jet Gram constants, variable-coefficient source defects and cancellation, exact simple-pole support and the separate interior freezing defect. The support diagram shows a bound, not universal nonvanishing.
